Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle sampling evidence for SuperLedger usage allocation

Rajiv / Finance team,

We noticed a mid-cycle usage jump on Oct 21 tied to requests routed through the streaming connector. Your invoice (attached) shows a ~37k token increase over baseline for the Oct 1–21 window. Before we escalate this to collections, can you confirm whether the spike was expected on your end (batch replay, import, or an SDK rollout)?

To speed reconciliation, could you attach a short sample of request ids and token counts (CSV) from Oct 21 covering the 09:00–12:00 ET window? If you have a trace (request id -> session id) that would help us map sessions vs. replay.

We're also going to pull the server-side sampling logs on our side to verify whether any prefix replay or duplicate ingestion occurred. If this looks like a one-off replay we can propose a mid-cycle credit and adjust the Oct invoice; if it's a systemic issue we'll work on a longer-term fix.

Next steps suggested:
- SuperLedger: send sample CSV (request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) for 09:00–12:00 ET Oct 21
- Redwood billing ops: run sampling-window diff and return token attribution breakdown
- Both: agree on credit if duplication/replay confirmed

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter

Hi Ben,

Thanks for flagging this. We saw the same spike in our dashboards and traced it to a consumer job that replayed a backlog of messages to a dev cluster (mistaken environment variable). The job started at ~08:47 ET and ran for about 2.5hrs.

I've attached a short export for the 09:00–12:00 ET window as requested: superledger-usage-sample-20261021.csv. The CSV includes request_id, timestamp_utc, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, session_tag. Quick notes from our side:
- The replay originated from worker wkr-7 (internal) and was intended for staging
- We see duplicated request_ids for a small subset (~2.8%) where a retry loop in the connector retried without idempotency keys

We don't have visibility into Redwood's sampling window logic; if you can confirm how prefix caching and streaming sampling interacts with replays that would help us agree on an adjustment.

Attaching: superledger-usage-sample-20261021.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Best,
Rajiv

Subject: RE: Fwd: Mid-cycle sampling evidence for SuperLedger usage allocation

Ben / Rajiv / Billing Ops,

We completed the sampling-window diff and manual verification against the attached CSV. Summary of findings:

- Root cause: connector replay + missing idempotency caused ~2.8% duplicated request_ids during the 09:00–12:00 ET window. Our streaming ingestion deduplication runs at two stages: immediate request-id dedupe (best-effort) and a rolling-window aggregator for session stitching. The replay volume and the retry timing fell between those two layers, so duplicates were counted once in the immediate pass but re-counted during the rolling-window aggregation for billing.
- Token impact: gross additional billed tokens = 37,490 tokens. After applying our dedupe correction (we remove duplicates and attribute unique tokens to the earlier timestamp), net overcount = 32,450 tokens.
- Credit proposal: we propose a pro-rated credit of $3,450 (based on SL-9872 rate tier and prorated window). We've applied the adjustment to the Oct 1 invoice; revised invoice link below and an updated PDF attached.

Action items completed:
- Issued credit: $3,450 (applied to invoice-20261001-superledger.pdf)
- Invoice updated in billing system: https://drive.google.com/superledger/invoice-20261001 (rev 1)
- Notified collections to hold any escalation pending confirmation from SuperLedger finance

Rajiv: if SuperLedger can confirm the replay path (worker id and pipeline) we can add a tagging rule to prevent cross-environment replays from counting toward production usage (suggested change: require env-id header on requests and ignore requests with env-id != production). Happy to coordinate a short RFC with platform engineering.

Marissa / Jordan: please confirm credit reflected in AR and close this ticket.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Finance Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
